No components found.
Radio (radio)
Source: docs/components/atoms/radio/radio.examples.json

Example: Standalone radio
A single labeled radio outside a group.
    <Radio label="Email" name="contact-method" value="email" />

Example: Label-less table radio
Row selection where the row content already provides visible context, described instead by aria-label.
    <Radio aria-label="Select primary matter" name="matter-radio" value="primary" defaultChecked />

Example: Disabled
A non-interactive option.
    <Radio label="Overnight" name="delivery-speed" value="overnight" disabled />

Example: Controlled RadioGroup
Single selection driven by external state via the options API.
    <RadioGroup label="Preferred contact method" name="contact-method" value={value} onValueChange={setValue} options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'phone', label: 'Phone' }, { value: 'mail', label: 'Mail' }]} />

Example: Uncontrolled RadioGroup
Single selection with an initial value, owned by the native fieldset.
    <RadioGroup label="Delivery speed" name="delivery-speed" defaultValue="standard" options={[{ value: 'standard', label: 'Standard' }, { value: 'expedited', label: 'Expedited' }, { value: 'overnight', label: 'Overnight' }]} />

Example: RadioGroup with children composition
A custom layout of manually-wired Radio instances, used instead of the options API.
    <RadioGroup label="Status" name="status" description="Grouped manually instead of using the options API"><Radio label="Draft" name="status" value="draft" defaultChecked /><Radio label="In review" name="status" value="in-review" /><Radio label="Final" name="status" value="final" /></RadioGroup>

Example: Horizontal orientation
Options laid out in a row that wraps rather than overflowing.
    <RadioGroup label="Delivery speed" name="delivery-speed" orientation="horizontal" defaultValue="standard" options={[{ value: 'standard', label: 'Standard' }, { value: 'expedited', label: 'Expedited' }, { value: 'overnight', label: 'Overnight' }]} />

Example: Required RadioGroup
A required group-level question, with the indicator shown after the legend.
    <RadioGroup label="Preferred contact method" name="contact-method" required options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'phone', label: 'Phone' }]} />

Example: Invalid RadioGroup with error message
Invalid state paired with a visible, described error rather than color alone.
    <RadioGroup label="Preferred contact method" name="contact-method" invalid errorMessage="Choose one option before continuing." options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'phone', label: 'Phone' }]} />

Example: Disabled RadioGroup
Every generated option is disabled together.
    <RadioGroup label="Preferred contact method" name="contact-method" disabled defaultValue="email" options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'phone', label: 'Phone' }]} />

Don't: Loose radios wired by hand
The set has no legend, and every radio needs its own name and checked logic. Use RadioGroup's options, which shares the name and keeps the value for you.
    <Radio name="method" value="email" label="Email" checked={method === 'email'} onCheckedChange={() => setMethod('email')} />
    <Radio name="method" value="phone" label="Phone" checked={method === 'phone'} onCheckedChange={() => setMethod('phone')} />

Don't: Marking one option required
The browser still asks for an answer, but the * looks as if only that option is required. Set required on the group, which puts the * after the legend.
    <RadioGroup label="Preferred contact method" options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email', required: true }, { value: 'phone', label: 'Phone' }]} />

Don't: Invalid with no message
The red circles alone don't say what's wrong, and not everyone can see the color. Pair invalid with an errorMessage that explains the problem.
    <RadioGroup label="Preferred contact method" invalid options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'phone', label: 'Phone' }]} />

Don't: Radios for independent choices
Radios allow exactly one answer. When any number of options can apply, use Checkbox (Checkbox Group).
    <RadioGroup label="Send matter updates by" options={[{ value: 'email', label: 'Email' }, { value: 'sms', label: 'SMS' }]} />
